common.aboutText: ATR brings together road sector professionals around technical expertise, safety, and sustainable infrastructure development.
common.committeesText: Four working axes structure ATR's action to contribute to the improvement of the Tunisian road network.
common.cooperationText: ATR works closely with its national and international partners to promote best practices in the road sector.

about.title: A technical organization dedicated to the Tunisian road network.
about.lead: Founded in 2018, the Tunisian Road Association brings together public officials, engineers, construction companies, academics, and experts around technical innovation, quality, and infrastructure safety.
about.body: ATR is presided over by Mrs. Lilia Sifaoui, General Director of the Bizerte New Bridge Management Unit. It works in close collaboration with the Ministry of Equipment and Housing and represents Tunisia within PIARC.
about.caption1: Tunisian Road Association — institutional visual of ATR.
about.history_title: A trajectory rooted in technical exchange
about.history_1_text: Birth of the Tunisian association dedicated to scientific and professional exchanges on roads.
about.history_2_text: PIARC, international partner of ATR, is founded as the World Road Association.
about.history_3_text: ATR connects administration, construction, engineering, laboratories, and universities around tangible projects.
about.mission_title: Uniting the expertise that builds roads.
about.mission_body: ATR provides a platform for dialogue among stakeholders who design, build, maintain, and study road infrastructure. It fosters method sharing, quality standards enforcement, and translating research into operational solutions.
about.hss_body: The 'Vision Zero Fatalities' approach places human life protection at the core of design, operation, and prevention decisions.
about.pillar1_text: Mitigate risks for road users, operators, and construction work crews.
about.pillar2_text: Disseminate health, safety, and quality practices aligned with international standards.
about.pillar3_text: Design infrastructures that minimize the consequences of human error.
about.activity1_text: Gather public, private, and academic stakeholders around technical challenges of the road network.
about.activity2_text: Structure expertise working groups on design, safety, structures, and resilience.
about.activity3_text: Provide technical resources and field feedback for road sector professionals.
about.activity4_text: Connect Tunisian experts to the works of the World Road Association, founded in 1909.
about.ct1_text: Asset management, climate adaptation, and service continuity.
about.ct2_text: Data, connected mobility, corridor decarbonization, and intermodality.
about.ct3_text: Safety audits, black spot mitigation, and road hazard prevention.
about.ct4_text: Pavement design, monitoring, bridge maintenance, and recycled materials.
about.governance_title: A governance open to all sector colleges.
about.governance_body: The Steering Committee gathers key disciplines required for an evidence-based and actionable road policy.
about.college1_text: Public officials and road administration representatives.
about.college2_text: Public works contractors and implementation stakeholders.
about.college3_text: Design, engineering, and technical assistance capabilities.
about.college4_text: Applied research, testing, education, and knowledge transfer.
about.piarc_note: PIARC enables Tunisian members to access international research, compare practices, and contribute to World Road Association forums.
about.caption2: ATR technical seminar — knowledge exchange among road professionals.
about.join_text: To learn about membership procedures and activities open to professionals, contact ATR.

domaines.title: Domains driven by identified challenges and expertise.
domaines.intro: ATR structures its activities around safety, civil engineering structures, and technical excellence. Each domain connects an operational mission, action axes, and accessible resources.
domaines.domain1_mission: ATR translates the 'Vision Zero' approach into preventive methods applicable to infrastructures and work zones. The domain connects hazard analysis, audits, signage, and HSS training.
domaines.domain1_action2: Training & workshops on work zone safety
domaines.domain2_mission: This domain covers the design, inspection, monitoring, and sustainable maintenance of bridges and civil engineering structures.
domaines.domain2_action1: Monitoring and asset management of bridges
domaines.domain3_mission: ATR aligns regulatory standards, engineering methods, and operational requirements of the road network. It promotes technical guides and international best practices.
domaines.facts_desc: The displayed data distinguishes institutional facts from figures that require further confirmation.
domaines.note_text: The exact number of active members and total published guides are awaiting single official validation and are thus not listed as finalized figures.

formation.hero_title: Building skills for safer and more resilient roads.
formation.hero_lead: The ATR Academy provides professional continuing education for engineers, technicians, public officials, and contractors. Dates and modalities are confirmed upon request.
formation.caption: Road design visual — Academy sessions emphasize hands-on real-world application.
formation.format1_text: A structured program featuring pedagogical progression, formal evaluation, and certification.
formation.format2_text: Short sessions centered on practical problems, standard methods, and case studies.
formation.programs_title: Clear curriculum details prior to enrollment
formation.programs_intro: As upcoming dates are announced progressively, each program card clarifies prerequisites and terms.
formation.prog1_audience: Engineers, public officials, and road engineering specialists.
formation.prog1_prereq: Prerequisite: experience or degree in road infrastructure.
formation.prog1_desc: Structured around risk hazard identification, safety audit procedures, and 'Vision Zero'. Evaluation modalities are provided upon registration.
formation.prog2_audience: Design engineers, technicians, and civil contractors.
formation.prog2_prereq: Prerequisite: fundamentals of road design & materials.
formation.prog2_desc: A practical session dedicated to pavement dimensioning methods, pavement data interpretation, and Tunisian technical specifications.
formation.prog3_audience: Public planners, design offices, engineers, and researchers.
formation.prog3_desc: A workshop to integrate flood, heat, and slope stability hazards into road design, asset management, and preventative maintenance.
formation.calendar_title: See sessions listed in the agenda
formation.calendar_text: Confirmed dates are centralized in the official calendar.
formation.faq1_a: Submit your inquiry via the Contact form specifying the selected program. Our secretariat will provide registration requirements and dates.
formation.faq2_a: Access rules vary per program. Contact ATR to explore terms and potential member advantages.
formation.faq3_a: Certification cycles include formal evaluations and credentials. Practical workshops provide attendance attestations.
formation.cta_title: Build your learning path with ATR
formation.cta_text: Request the full syllabus, admission criteria, and upcoming schedules from the secretariat.
